Cross-Platform Build Matrix Overview

sci (the SA compiler) is built with the Zig build system, and build.zig.zon requires Zig 0.17.0. The table below lists all targets verified to pass (stock Zig 0.17.0, a Linux x86_64 host; the main branch already includes the full multi-platform runtime from the cross-platform branch):

TargetTripleCommandProducts
Linux x86_64 (native)x86_64-linux-gnu (default)zig build (needs LLVM 14; see Local Builds on Linux and Windows)zig-out/bin/sa (about 20M), libsa_std.a/.so
Windows x86_64x86_64-windows-gnuzig build -Dtarget=x86_64-windows-gnu -Dllvm=falsesa.exe (about 11M), hubproxy.exe
ARM Linuxaarch64-linux-gnuzig build -Dtarget=aarch64-linux-gnu -Dllvm=falseARM aarch64 ELF (verifiable with file)
macOS ARMaarch64-macoszig build -Dtarget=aarch64-macos -Dllvm=falseMach-O arm64 sa + libsa_std.dylib
macOS Intelx86_64-macoszig build -Dtarget=x86_64-macos -Dllvm=falseSame as above, x86_64 Mach-O
FreeBSD x86_64x86_64-freebsdsh tools/build_freebsd.sh (needs a sysroot; see the FreeBSD Cross-Compilation page)FreeBSD 14.4 ELF (interpreter /libexec/ld-elf.so.1)

General notes:

  • -Dllvm=false disables the LLVM-C backend (cross targets can only do this; native Windows is the exception, and native Linux enables it by default). When it is disabled, llvmc-related tests are skipped/fail, which is expected behavior.
  • -p <directory> can change the install prefix from the default zig-out/ to elsewhere; note that the sa-std-runtime test requires the default zig-out/lib to exist, so running that test after building with -p reports FileNotFound; running a default zig build once restores it.
  • A build also syncs products into the source tree at artifacts/sa_std/libsa_std.a (a git-tracked file); if you are only verifying locally, restore it after building with git checkout -- artifacts/sa_std/libsa_std.a, to avoid mixing local build products into a commit.
NoteCross-compilation only proves that “compile + link” passes. The behavioral correctness of each target still needs to be confirmed by running the corresponding test suite on real hardware (or QEMU / Wine, etc.).
